preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 1000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 1000) representing the number of test cases.
For each test case, the first line contains two space-separated integers N and K (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5, 1 ≤ K ≤ N) representing the length of S and the number of partitions, respectively.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) == N for N, line in zip([int(stdin.split()[i*2+1]) for i in range(T)], stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line is a string S of length N containing only lowercase Latin letters.
The sum of N over all test cases does not exceed 2 * 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.splitlines()) == T, stdout.splitlines() == [output for _, _, output in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1::2], stdin.splitlines()[2::2], stdout.splitlines())])
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case, where each line is the lexicographically smallest string S' formed by partitioning S into exactly K non-empty subsequences and concatenating them.

postconditions.expression: all(len(S) == N and K >= 1 and K <= N and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in S) for N, S in zip([int(stdin.split()[i*2+1]) for i in range(T)], stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the input string S is of length N, contains only lowercase Latin letters, and K is a valid partition count (1 ≤ K ≤ N).

postconditions.expression: all(len(S_prime) == N and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in S_prime) for S_prime in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output string S' is of length N and contains only lowercase Latin letters.

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[::K]) if K == 1 else True for S_prime, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: If K == 1, the output S' is exactly the input string S (since no partitioning is needed).

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S)) if K == N else True for S_prime, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: If K == N, the output S' is the lexicographically smallest permutation of S (each character is its own subsequence).

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S)) if K == N else True for S_prime, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: The output S' is the lexicographically smallest string formed by partitioning S into K subsequences and concatenating them. This means that for any other valid partition into K subsequences, the concatenated result is not lexicographically smaller than S'.

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[::K]) if K == 1 else True for S_prime, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: The output S' is formed by partitioning S into K subsequences such that the concatenation is lexicographically smallest. This is achieved by grouping characters in a way that prioritizes smaller characters earlier in the string.

postconditions.expression: all(S_prime == ''.join(sorted(S)) if K == N else True for S_prime, S in zip(stdout.splitlines(), stdin.splitlines()[2::2]))
postconditions.description: The output S' is the lexicographically smallest string formed by partitioning S into K subsequences, where the subsequences are concatenated in order. This is equivalent to sorting the characters of S and distributing them into K subsequences in a way that minimizes the lexicographical order of the concatenated result.
